description:
We are Team Astro Intel, a group of passionate students interested in space exploration, astronomy, AI/ML, data science and technology. 
We aim to build innovative, practical solutions using NASA datasets. We welcome participants skilled or interested in Python, AI/ML, web development, GIS, UI/UX, 3D visualization, astronomy and research.
summary:
Mars Explorer AI is an autonomous, 100% offline Martian map, excursion planner, and life-support survival co-pilot developed by Team Astro Intel for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Challenge No. 10).
We developed a unified GIS cockpit fusing eight NASA/ESA datasets (MOLA, THEMIS, CRISM, SWIM/SHARAD, MSL RAD) with a sub-15 ms A* pathfinding engine, a live Marswalk EVA simulator, and MISA AI. MISA provides predictive compound-hazard warnings, data confidence ratings, landing zone scoring, and an In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) drilling planner.
The platform directly addresses Martian exploration challenges by overcoming 4–24 minute Earth radio delays, finite ~8-hour spacesuit oxygen and battery limits, lethal terrain hazards (steep scarps, boulders, -120°C cold, radiation), and >$200,000/kg Earth resupply costs. By running completely offline on habitat hardware, it routes astronauts safely around traps, enforces an inviolable 15% consumable return reserve, exports waypoints for scout rovers and wrist displays, and locates shallow subsurface water ice.
This is critical because current planetary tools rely on disconnected datasets, passive visuals, and Earth-based cloud links, leaving crews vulnerable during emergencies. Mars Explorer AI transforms raw orbital data into split-second, life-saving decisions, making sustainable human surface exploration and self-sustaining Martian habitats achievable.

🚀 NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — Project Details

Project Name: Mars Explorer AI

Challenge No. 10: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map

Team Name: Astro Intel (Mohali, India)

1. What does it do or how does it work?

Mars Explorer AI is an autonomous planetary exploration, survival navigation, and mission-planning platform designed for future astronauts on the surface of Mars. It transforms raw orbital remote-sensing datasets into an interactive, multi-layer decision cockpit:

  1. Dual-Grid Planetary Terrain Model: It maps 10×7 km10 \times 7\text{ km}10×7 km operational landing zones across three primary sites (Jezero Crater, Arcadia Planitia, and Korolev Crater) at a human-scale 16.6-metre16.6\text{-metre}16.6-metre resolution (252,000252,000252,000 points per site) using continuous typed arrays for maximum performance.
    • Shortest Route (direct metric distance)
    • Safest Route (penalizes slopes >12∘>12^\circ>12∘ and rock clusters, reducing fall hazard by >70%>70\%>70%)
    • Science Route (maximizes visits to craters and ancient clay/carbonate outcrops)
    • Water-Ice Route (follows shallow subsurface ice corridors)
  2. Physiological Marswalk EVA Simulator: Models real-time metabolic O2\text{O}_2O2​ draw (scaling with uphill terrain), suit battery heating drain in extreme sub-zero cold (down to −120∘C-120^\circ\text{C}−120∘C), and cumulative cosmic radiation.
  3. The 15% Inviolable Return Rule: At every single step, the simulator continuously projects return consumables. If the oxygen remaining after walking back to base drops below 15%15\%15%, it triggers an immediate Emergency Abort Alert and locks the fastest return vector to prevent astronaut stranding.
  4. MISA (Mars Intelligent Survival Assistant): An onboard AI decision engine that evaluates any selected coordinate, explaining why an area is dangerous, assessing touchdown landing safety, calculating drilling energy costs, and providing instant tactical advisories (PROCEED, CAUTION, ABORT).

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Guaranteed Astronaut Safety (Zero Stranding): Enforces strict life-support margins, preventing crew members from exceeding their point of safe return.
  • In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) Optimization: Pinpoints buried ice sheets (as shallow as 0.3–0.5 m0.3\text{--}0.5\text{ m}0.3–0.5 m at Arcadia Planitia) and calculates required drilling tools (hand auger vs. rotary percussion drill), energy consumption (kWh\text{kWh}kWh), and potable water yields (917 L/m3917\text{ L/m}^3917 L/m3).
  • Closed-Loop Rocket Fuel Synthesis: Automatically calculates the stoichiometric conversion of extracted water into breathing O2\text{O}_2O2​ (∼888 kg/m3\sim 888\text{ kg/m}^3∼888 kg/m3) and hydrogen for Sabatier methane (CH4\text{CH}_4CH4​) rocket fuel for the return flight to Earth.
  • 100% Offline Habitat Independence: Runs entirely in the client-side browser with zero server round-trips, meaning astronauts can plan excursions locally without being paralyzed by the 4-to-24-minute Mars-Earth communication delay.
  • Transparent Scientific Provenance: Features a site-aware Data Confidence Index that clearly distinguishes observed orbital observations from calibrated procedural models, ensuring scientific honesty and operational transparency.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Accelerating Human Mars Exploration: Directly supports NASA’s Moon-to-Mars architecture and future crewed surface missions (such as Starship and Artemis-derived surface habitats).
  • Paradigm Shift in Planetary Cartography: Transitions planetary mapping from passive, static satellite image viewing into an active, life-support-coupled survival cockpit.
  • Massive Cost Reduction: Transporting water from Earth costs upwards of $200,000 per kg\$200,000\text{ per kg}$200,000 per kg. By enabling astronauts to reliably locate, reach, and extract surface/subsurface ice, this platform significantly reduces mission launch mass and makes permanent planetary bases economically viable.
  • Operational Readiness for Habitat Crews: Bridges the gap between raw planetary science archives and mission operations, providing flight crews and ground controllers with flight-computer-ready JSON waypoint graphs and one-click Markdown EVA briefings.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Languages & Core Technologies: TypeScript, React 19, HTML5 Canvas API (for 60 FPS60\text{ FPS}60 FPS rendering of 252,000252,000252,000 elevation and hazard points), and Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG).
  • Frameworks & Routing: TanStack Start & TanStack Router (SSR/Nitro metadata generation), Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, and Radix UI primitives.
    • NASA MGS MOLA: Areocentric topography grids & slope matrices.
    • NASA Mars Odyssey THEMIS: Daytime/nighttime thermal IR & thermal inertia.
    • NASA MRO CRISM & ESA OMEGA: Hyperspectral mineralogy signatures.
    • Planetary Science Institute (PSI) SWIM Project & SHARAD: Dielectric subsurface water ice probability maps.
    • NASA MSL Curiosity RAD: Ground-level cosmic ray radiation baselines.
    • NASA MRO HiRISE & CTX: Sub-metre obstacle and boulder distribution baselines.
  • Hardware: Developed and optimized on standard laptops to ensure the engine runs smoothly on low-power, edge-computing habitat computers and astronaut tablet interfaces.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Compound Risk Explanation vs. Raw Numbers: Conventional GIS maps only display passive colors or numbers. Mars Explorer AI creatively models synergistic compound hazards—explaining that a 22∘22^\circ22∘ slope combined with −85∘C-85^\circ\text{C}−85∘C extreme cold and loose regolith creates a high-risk zone requiring climber tethers and accelerated battery budgets.
  • Connecting Satellite Pixels to the Drill Bit: Instead of simply marking "ice exists here," our platform calculates the engineering physics of extraction: overburden thickness, required hand vs. powered drill equipment, operational hours, electrical energy (kWh\text{kWh}kWh), and exact chemical yields of water and rocket propellant.
  • Life-Support as a Routing Constraint: Pathfinding algorithms usually only minimize distance or time. Our A* engine creatively integrates astronaut physiology—treating spacesuit O2\text{O}_2O2​ capacity, metabolic incline exertion, and radiation exposure as non-negotiable cost penalties.
  • Dual Design Systems for Extreme Environments: Created both a high-contrast dark cockpit HUD and a crisp white/light theme designed to remain legible whether viewed inside a lit habitat, on an astronaut's wrist terminal, or projected onto helmet visors.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Human Physiological Limits: We accounted for the physical strain of walking in a pressurized suit. Incline gradients dramatically increase metabolic O2\text{O}_2O2​ draw, and sub-zero temperatures force heaters to drain suit batteries up to 45%45\%45% faster.
    • Jezero: Water chemically bound in clay minerals requiring thermal dehydration.
    • Arcadia Planitia: Shallow excess ice sheets (<1 m<1\text{ m}<1 m) ideal for early landing and hand-auger extraction.
    • Korolev Crater: A massive 1.8 km1.8\text{ km}1.8 km thick glacial ice dome representing a permanent colony reservoir.
  • Scientific Honesty & Verification: We carefully differentiated between empirical satellite observations and calibrated procedural models. We built 141414 automated unit tests into our pipeline to ensure that pathfinding never routes through impassable terrain and that consumable equations strictly respect safety thresholds.
